name: The Weight of It
intro:
A collection exploring what we hold onto, what holds us, and the emotional weight of familiar structures.
Rendered in stark, heavy compositions and simplified imagery, this piece balances comfort with enclosure. The heavy, grounding forms invite the viewer to reflect on the familiar things we carry that make us feel held, while capturing the quiet tension when that same weight begins to close in.

name: Nowhere, Elsewhere
intro:
Nowhere, Elsewhere begins with fragments gathered from years of observing Delhi - trees, horizons, colour and experiences, but deliberately removes them from their original surroundings.
Watercolour, ink and typewritten poetry are layered to construct imaginedlandscapes that exist between memory and invention.
Familiar elements become part of places that feel recognisable without belonging anywhere in particular.

name: Light in Shade
intro:
The Light in Shade collection is inspired by the changing light beneath Delhi’s tree canopies.
This piece explores the fleeting beauty of a moment that cannot be held. Through bold colours, layered watercolour washes and ink brushwork, it captures the shifting interplay between light and shadow, transforming an observed landscape into a remembered experience.
Rather than capturing a physical location, this painting lingers on the feeling of passing through a space.

name: Be Here Now
intro:
The Be Here Now collection is an exploration of presence and the quiet richness of ordinary moments.
Drawing on the trees and green spaces of Delhi, this work uses bold, simplified forms and detailed graphic ink work to isolate and celebrate a familiar natural element.
Removed from its original surroundings and reimagined through stark color, the piece becomes less about a specific location and more about the simple act of paying attention.

name: Lost in the Line
intro:
The Lost in the Line series explores the underlying geometry, structure and texture of the world around us.
Through intricate line work, repeated patterns and the interplay of density and space, familiar forms are reduced to their essential structures. Working with little or no colour, these pieces invite a closer look at the lines, rhythms and details that often go unnoticed, revealing the complexity within the seemingly simple.
